Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 3ed21c1451a14d139e1ceb18f2fa70865ce3195a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2021 13:33:37 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] vdpa: check that offsets are within bounds

In this function "c->off" is a u32 and "size" is a long.  On 64bit systems
if "c->off" is greater than "size" then "size - c->off" is a negative and
we always return -E2BIG.  But on 32bit systems the subtraction is type
promoted to a high positive u32 value and basically any "c->len" is
accepted.

Fixes: 4c8cf31885f6 ("vhost: introduce vDPA-based backend")
Reported-by: Xie Yongji <xieyongji@bytedance.com>
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211208103337.GA4047@kili
Signed-off-by: Michael S. Tsirkin <mst@redhat.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

diff --git a/drivers/vhost/vdpa.c b/drivers/vhost/vdpa.c
index 29cced1cd277..e3c4f059b21a 100644
--- a/drivers/vhost/vdpa.c
+++ b/drivers/vhost/vdpa.c
@@ -197,7 +197,7 @@ static int vhost_vdpa_config_validate(struct vhost_vdpa *v,
 	struct vdpa_device *vdpa = v->vdpa;
 	long size = vdpa->config->get_config_size(vdpa);
 
-	if (c->len == 0)
+	if (c->len == 0 || c->off > size)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	if (c->len > size - c->off)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/vhost/vdpa.c`**
   - The condition in the `vhost_vdpa_config_validate` function was modified. 
   - The original check `if (c->len == 0)` was updated to `if (c->len == 0 || c->off > size)`. 
   - This change ensures that if `c->off` exceeds the `size`, the function will return an error (`-EINVAL`), preventing invalid configurations.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `vdpa.c` addresses a bug related to the handling of offsets in the configuration validation process. The original logic allowed for potentially invalid configurations on 32-bit systems due to type promotion during subtraction, which could lead to accepting out-of-bounds offsets. By adding the check for `c->off > size`, the patch ensures that both the length and the offset are validated against the size, thus improving the robustness of the function across different architectures. This change is directly related to the reported issue and aims to fix the inconsistency in behavior between 32-bit and 64-bit systems.

        Root cause:
        The bug arises from the handling of the `c->off` offset, which is a `u32`, and the `size`, which is a `long`. On 64-bit systems, if `c->off` exceeds `size`, the subtraction results in a negative value, leading to a consistent error return of `-E2BIG`. However, on 32-bit systems, the subtraction is type promoted to a high positive `u32` value, allowing invalid configurations to pass through without error. This inconsistency in offset validation between architectures is the root cause of the bug.
        
        Commit message:

we always return -E2BIG.  But on 32bit systems the subtraction is type

accepted.

Fixes: 4c8cf31885f6 ("vhost: introduce vDPA-based backend")
Reported-by: Xie Yongji <xieyongji@bytedance.com>
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211208103337.GA4047@kili

 static int vhost_vdpa_config_validate(struct vhost_vdpa *v,
 				      struct vhost_vdpa_config *c)
 {

 	long size = vdpa->config->get_config_size(vdpa);

+	if (c->len == 0 || c->off > size)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	if (c->len > size - c->off)
 		return -E2BIG;
 
 	return 0;
 }
